indicators.label: Doomsday Clock, seconds to midnight
indicators.note: Announced 27 Jan 2026: 85 seconds to midnight, the closest the Clock has ever been set. Down from 89 seconds in 2025.

indicators.label: Global nuclear warhead inventory
indicators.source_name: Federation of American Scientists, Nuclear Notebook
indicators.note: Nine countries held roughly 12,187 warheads as of early 2026 (military stockpile plus retired warheads awaiting dismantlement). FAS's own page states 12,321 in body text elsewhere; this uses the structured summary-table figure.

indicators.label: State-based conflict deaths per 100,000 people
indicators.note: UCDP does not publish a per-100,000 rate directly. Computed here from UCDP's reported 94,700 state-based battle-related deaths in 2025 divided by approximate world population (~8.2 billion), ahead of the formal GED v26.1 dataset release. Treat as an approximation.

indicators.label: Active state-based armed conflicts
indicators.note: 65 state-based armed conflicts in 2025, the highest number since UCDP records began in 1946. Sourced from UCDP's official summary press release; the underlying dataset file (v26.1) was not accessed directly. This is also the first indicator to exceed its own anchor_max of 60, so it now scores the maximum 100.

indicators.label: Forcibly displaced people, share of world population
indicators.note: 117.8 million forcibly displaced at end-2025, about 1.4% of world population. Direct PDF fetch returned an access error; figure cross-confirmed via independent summaries of the same report but not verified against the PDF text directly.

indicators.label: Atmospheric CO₂, Mauna Loa monthly mean
indicators.note: Raw monthly mean, July 2026. NOAA flags the most recent year of data as preliminary pending recalibration.

indicators.label: Global surface temperature anomaly vs 1880–1899
indicators.note: NASA publishes 2025 as +1.19°C vs. its default 1951–1980 baseline. Re-based here to 1880–1899 using NASA's own table (1880–1899 mean of -0.225°C vs. 1951–1980), giving +1.42°C. This re-basing is a derived calculation, not an official NASA-published figure for this exact window.

indicators.label: Living Planet Index, 1970 = 100
indicators.note: Latest published edition (2024 report) reports monitored wildlife populations averaging 27 on the 1970 = 100 scale, a 73% average decline. No newer edition found as of Aug 2026 (biennial cadence). Stale: underlying data runs only through 2020.

indicators.label: World military expenditure as share of global GDP
indicators.note: World military expenditure reached 2.5% of global GDP in 2025, the highest level since 2009.

indicators.label: Ratio of world military expenditure to official development assistance
indicators.source_name: SIPRI Military Expenditure Database + OECD DAC
indicators.note: Computed as world military expenditure ($2,887bn, SIPRI 2025) divided by total official development assistance ($174.3bn, OECD DAC 2025, preliminary — https://www.oecd.org/en/data/insights/data-explainers/2026/04/a-historic-decline-in-foreign-aid-preliminary-2025-oda-data.html). ODA fell 23.1% year-on-year, the largest annual contraction on record; final revised 2025 ODA figures are due around December 2026.

indicators.label: Top 1%'s share of global wealth
indicators.source_name: World Inequality Lab, World Inequality Report 2026
indicators.note: Added in methodology v1.1. The top 1% held 37% of global personal wealth in 2025 (top 10% held 75%, bottom 50% held 2%), per the World Inequality Report 2026 (Piketty, Zucman, Chancel et al.), published December 2025. Not annual — the World Inequality Report is published roughly every 3-4 years (prior editions 2018, 2022). anchor_max (70%) is the United Kingdom's 1914 national wealth concentration, the most extreme level documented in the World Inequality Database's long-run series -- no reliable global historical extreme exists, since the World Inequality Lab itself states a global wealth-distribution estimate before roughly 1980 is not reliable.

indicators.label: RSF World Press Freedom global score
indicators.note: RSF states 2026 is the lowest average score in the Index's 25-year history but does not publish a single blended global figure as page text. This value is self-computed as the unweighted mean of all 180 published country scores on RSF's 2026 Index page — a derived figure, not a directly quoted RSF statistic.

indicators.label: V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index, population-weighted
indicators.note: The population-weighted global Liberal Democracy Index for 2025 is published only as a chart image in the Democracy Report 2026, not as extractable text. Approximated here from the report's stated '30% decline from the 2003 peak of 0.39' (0.39 × 0.70 ≈ 0.27). The separately reported unweighted country average is roughly 0.37 (about 10% below its 2012 peak of 0.41).

indicators.label: Global DTP3 immunisation coverage
indicators.note: Global DTP3 coverage was 85% in 2024 (about 109 million infants), per the WHO/UNICEF joint 2024-revision estimates released 15 July 2025. Revised figures, not provisional.

indicators.label: World population in extreme poverty
indicators.note: 9% of world population (713 million people) below $2.15/day (2017 PPP) in 2022, the latest year with a survey-based (non-nowcast) estimate on this line. September 2024 revised update. Stale: reference year is about four years old. The World Bank switched its primary poverty line to $3.00/day (2021 PPP) in June 2025 but retains this legacy series for comparability.
